Q30165884.summary: This small bronze belt plate is worked in openwork within a border of leaves: a frontal figure with a large, mask-like head and outstretched arms appears above a long-bodied quadruped, accompanied by birds and stylized animal heads. Wikidata identifies the scene, with a question mark, as Christ riding the donkey. Such buckles, worn by men and women of the early medieval kingdoms north of the Alps, show how Christian images were absorbed into local ornament.
facts: A bronze buckle plate of the same period in the Musée d'Art et d'Histoire, Geneva (also in this collection), is identified by that museum as Christ's Entry into Jerusalem.
The buckle is displayed in the Cantonal Museum of Archaeology and History in Lausanne's Palais de Rumine.
Q30165884.notes: Identification as Christ rests only on the Wikidata description ('featuring Christ on his donkey (?)'); the figure is highly stylized and could be another subject (other buckles of this family show e.g. Daniel or riders). No museum record was found; date taken from Wikidata (6th century) broadened to 6th–7th. Scripture omitted because the subject is uncertain.
